lines: {target}? Empty End stone gives no comfort. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for End Barrens, tell them. Keep away from edges and watch the sky. I will be at the bell.
The void makes silence feel heavier. I'll remember that from near the bell.
End Barrens is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember End Barrens as bare End land with nothing friendly in sight. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
I would remember End Barrens because of wind crossing the bare island. My ears keep better notes than I do.
At End Barrens, I would measure distance in snacks. Three snacks is not nearby.
I would not trade the last loaf for a souvenir from End Barrens. Please remind me I said that.
Once the light changed at End Barrens, I would stop calling one more look a small delay.
If someone needed help at End Barrens, I would fetch the sensible people and remember where they went.
I would ask what flat purple light meant for the trip. Guessing at conditions has gone badly before.
Good light might help me avoid an unmarked edge above the void. That is worth the extra torches.
I would wonder how the bare end stone with almost nothing growing came to be there, then remember I need not find out.
At End Barrens, if carrying loot made it harder to deal with an unmarked edge above the void, I would leave the loot. I hope.
Is End Barrens worth the walk? That depends on how much you enjoy walking back.
At End Barrens, I could spend too long staring at the bare end stone with almost nothing growing. Someone sensible should tug my sleeve.
I would wave at End Barrens when leaving. I wave at places sometimes. They rarely wave back.
I know the sound people make when I miss a sign. I hope not to hear it while dealing with an unmarked edge above the void.
A strange smell near the bare end stone with almost nothing growing would send me back toward the route back to the gateway.
I have no clever trick for an enderman on the empty ground. Leaving is a trick I can usually manage.
{target}? High End ground still ends in void. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for End Highlands, tell them. Mind bridges and do not chase anything floating. I will be at the bell.
Chorus fruit grows where falling is easy. I'll remember that from near the bell.
End Highlands is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember End Highlands as high ground that does not feel safe. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
At End Highlands, I would place lights where they pointed home, not where they looked pretty.
Bad conditions at End Highlands would make every direction convincing. That is dangerous for me.
On the way back from End Highlands, I would follow our marks instead of inventing a better route.
If someone needed help at End Highlands, I would fetch the sensible people and remember where they went.
The moment a wide gap between high ledges became a problem, I would stop. Obvious things have a habit of escaping me.
Bringing blocks, food, and an ender pearl sounds sensible for End Highlands. I should write that down before I pack biscuits.
Strange places dislike idle hands. I can carry the food bag and keep mine busy.
I can get lost near my own bed, so End Highlands deserves proper caution.
I would keep looking back at the gateway on the high ground. A way out looks different from the wrong side.
I would let whatever was moving settle before choosing a path.
I wonder whether chorus branches moving nearby would seem louder when everyone stopped talking. I am rarely first to stop.
A heavy pack is poor company on the return from End Highlands.
End Highlands would make me curious. It would also make me glad someone else knows when to stop.
Why does chorus fruit and end stone always sound more harmless than it looks?
The trip home deserves daylight too, even if the interesting part used all of it.
{target}? Even the middle of the End feels lost. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for End Midlands, tell them. Mark your way and distrust the horizon. I will be at the bell.
There is no village smell in that air. I'll remember that from near the bell.
End Midlands is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember End Midlands as End stone stretching where roads should be. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
I would take an uneven ledge above the void seriously, even if I had just said something very unserious.
If flat purple light made the marked climb toward the gateway hard to see, finding it again would feel wonderful.
At End Midlands, I would tie everything twice. Loose laces have excellent timing.
Bringing blocks, food, and an ender pearl would make End Midlands less foolish. I would still provide foolishness on my own.
Once the light changed at End Midlands, I would stop calling one more look a small delay.
I would want to see the sloped end stone between high islands up close. Wanting and doing are different, according to annoyed friends.
Before exploring the sloped end stone between high islands, I would make everyone agree to meet at the marked climb toward the gateway.
I do not need every shiny thing near the sloped end stone between high islands. I have nowhere sensible to put most of them.
If my legs started wobbling near the sloped end stone between high islands, I would listen to them for once.
I can get lost near my own bed, so End Midlands deserves proper caution.
I might be wrong about End Midlands. I would prefer to be wrong from a safe spot.
I pack bread for danger and carrots for thinking. I am not sure either works, but they travel well.
I would find the marked climb toward the gateway before going farther. I lose directions more often than chalk.
A map of End Midlands would help, especially with a large drawing of the marked climb toward the gateway.
Someone should walk behind me at End Midlands. I stop for interesting nonsense without warning.
{target}? Small islands feel smaller beside the void. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for Small End Islands, tell them. Bridge slowly and never look proud near an edge. I will be at the bell.
End stone gives no second chances below it. I'll remember that from near the bell.
Small End Islands is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember Small End Islands as little bits of ground with forever around them. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
Bringing blocks, food, and an ender pearl would make Small End Islands less foolish. I would still provide foolishness on my own.
People become strange around treasure. I prefer the kind of strange that keeps both hands free.
I would wave at Small End Islands when leaving. I wave at places sometimes. They rarely wave back.
The moment a gap wider than it first looks became a problem, I would stop. Obvious things have a habit of escaping me.
I would point at the last solid island on the route three times and still ask whether everyone saw it.
At Small End Islands, helping someone might mean staying put where they can find me.
Has anyone counted how many ways a gap wider than it first looks can become a problem? I would stop at one.
If a souvenir hissed, moved, or glowed too brightly, it could stay at Small End Islands.
I would let whatever was moving settle before choosing a path.
When I told the story of Small End Islands, I would mention a gap wider than it first looks before the funny part.
If the light failed near the tiny islands scattered over the void, I would not pretend my eyes had adjusted.
I touch things while thinking. Near the tiny islands scattered over the void, I would try thinking with my hands in my pockets.
Traveling alone gives my ideas too much authority. Small End Islands deserves a group decision.
Someone else can learn whether an enderman on the next island is friendly. I already have a guess.
Bad conditions at Small End Islands would make every direction convincing. That is dangerous for me.
{target}? Victory there still feels far from home. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for The End, tell them. Don't anger the tall ones and keep away from the void. I will be at the bell.
End stone does not smell like any living place. I'll remember that from near the bell.
The End is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember The End as a pale world with no proper village sound. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
Traveling alone gives my ideas too much authority. The End deserves a group decision.
At The End, I would place lights where they pointed home, not where they looked pretty.
If I could no longer see the return portal near the center clearly, I would call that a warning.
People become strange around treasure. I prefer the kind of strange that keeps both hands free.
We should meet at the return portal near the center. Otherwise I might wait somewhere memorable only to me.
After The End, resting on the way home counts too. Stories make home feel closer than it is.
I would look closely at obsidian and end stone without picking up anything I did not understand. Experience taught me that.
Strange places dislike idle hands. I can carry the food bag and keep mine busy.
Nobody puts smells on a map. That seems careless when a bad smell can find you first.
Perhaps I am wrong about the central island and obsidian pillars. I am also perhaps excellent with directions.
At The End, I trust a map until it disagrees with the path. Then I trust whoever packed lunch.
Coming home from The End with no grand discovery would still count as coming home.
The End sounds impressive when people mention the central island and obsidian pillars. The trip home sounds less impressive.
The End would make me curious. It would also make me glad someone else knows when to stop.
I would remember The End because of dragon wings above the island. My ears keep better notes than I do.
{target}? Nothing below is not the same as safety. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for The Void, tell them. Stay away from edges like they owe you emeralds. I will be at the bell.
There is no road back from falling forever. I'll remember that from near the bell.
The Void is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember The Void as empty dark where even warnings feel small. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
If I could still reach the last solid island, I would call myself only partly lost. That is better than usual.
I would carry more light to The Void than seemed necessary. Necessary moves after sunset.
Stories never mention almost no sound at all in enough detail. They leave out useful things like that.
I would look closely at end stone without picking up anything I did not understand. Experience taught me that.
If I stumbled around end stone, I would check my boots before blaming the ground.
The village has fewer surprises than The Void. This is one of its finest qualities.
I would warn the group about an enderman standing at the edge, preferably before my voice became a squeak.
A shared meeting place is useful because yelling directions has never improved mine.
Coming home from The Void with no grand discovery would still count as coming home.
Curiosity could pull me toward the empty space between islands. A sensible hand on my shoulder could pull harder.
I can sound certain at The Void without being certain. The group should know in advance.
Strange places dislike idle hands. I can carry the food bag and keep mine busy.
I would ask a competent traveler to check that I brought blocks, food, and an ender pearl. They may check the rest too.
Slow steps near end stone sound dull. Dull steps tend to reach home.
The far side of the empty space between islands can stay far. I need not stand on every side of everything.
